title: POC scoping — Peregrine Analytics security gates & benchmark playbook
summary: Kickoff scoping for a 2-week proof-of-concept focused on security gates and benchmark acceptance. Discussed SOC 2/ISO expectations, SSO/SAML and RBAC integration, audit log retention, and concrete throughput/latency benchmarks for Peregrine's chat summarization workload.
topics: Security controls: SOC 2, ISO 27001, SSO/SAML, RBAC, audit logs
Workload sizing: concurrency, token profiles, expected qps
Benchmark plan: synthetic vs replay, metrics to capture
Timeline and next steps for pilot
next_steps: Redwood to share security pack (SOC 2 table, ISO summary, KMS notes) by 2026-02-15
SE to run a baseline synthetic benchmark with P99 and tokens/sec by 2026-02-18
Peregrine to provide sample dataset (anonymized) and success criteria doc by 2026-02-16
Schedule a 60-min benchmarking run and walkthrough week of 2026-02-23
action_items: Maya Chen: prepare benchmark harness and run initial synthetic load; due 2026-02-18
Jordan Patel: send security pack and pricing tiers; due 2026-02-15
Daniel Kim: upload anonymized sample telemetry and request profile to shared drive; due 2026-02-16
Priya Nair: confirm minimum audit log retention and any encryption-at-rest requirements; due 2026-02-17
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-02-12
Start: 15:00 PST
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Patel (Redwood AE), Maya Chen (Redwood SE), Liam O'Connor (Peregrine CTO), Priya Nair (Peregrine Head of Security), Daniel Kim (Peregrine ML Eng)

[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick intro, I'm Jordan on the account side, and Maya is our SE who will run the bench. Can you each do a 30-sec intro?
[00:12] Liam: Liam O'Connor, CTO, we run Peregrine's search and summarization infra. We're looking for a vendor to run a pilot to replace our home-grown inference stack.
[00:20] Priya: Hi, Priya Nair, head of security. I'll be validating compliance gates — SOC 2, ISO 27001 and any SSO or audit requirements.
[00:28] Daniel: Daniel Kim, ML. I'll own dataset and test harness, run integrations with our staging.
[00:35] Maya: Great. Goal for today: nail down success criteria, sizing, what benchmarks we run, and security checklist for the POC.

[02:05] Jordan: To set expectations: typical Redwood POC is two weeks of benching + a short integration window. We support hosted and private; you mentioned wanting VPC or private control plane?
[02:18] Liam: We prefer private deployment — VPC peering or on-prem — because of data residency and audit needs. But open to starting hosted if we can guarantee logs and encryption.
[02:28] Priya: For us SOC two is table stakes — SOC 2 Type II report, and we also need an ISO 27001 attestation. Can you provide both?
[02:36] Maya: Yes, we can share SOC 2 summary and ISO artifacts. Note our hosted offering uses customer KMS and supports Bring-Your-Own-Key in dedicated/private variants.
[03:05] Priya: Important: audit logs must capture request metadata, model version, token counts, user id (pseudonymized), and be retained 365 days. Is that configurable?
[03:18] Maya: Audit retention is configurable in Private and Dedicated; hosted default is 90 days but enterprise retention add-ons can extend. We can confirm retention SLA for the pilot.

[04:20] Daniel: On workload: our main flow is chat summarization. Typical request: 500 tokens input, 150 tokens output. Peak concurrency around 40 concurrent sessions, average QPS ~12, burst to 50 QPS for short periods. Monthly tokens ~120M.
[04:40] Maya: Okay that helps. For benching we'll test 1) steady-state 40 concurrency, 2) burst 50 qps, 3) long context tests at 2k tokens. What do you consider pass/fail for latency?
[04:55] Liam: P99 < 350ms for small requests (under 200 tokens), p95 < 200ms; for the 500/150 mix maybe p99 < 650ms. Cost target: below our internal $0.0008 per token for the current GPU fleet.
[05:20] Jordan: Good — we'll capture latency, tokens/sec, and unit cost. Also quality: we'll run a small diff test vs your current model outputs to ensure no regression in summarization F1/ROUGE scores.

[06:44] Priya: Security integration questions: we use Okta SAML SSO, SCIM for provisioning, and have RBAC rules that tie to AD groups. Can Redwood integrate via SAML and SCIM?
[06:56] Maya: Yes, SSO via SAML 2.0, SCIM provisioning both supported. RBAC mapping to AD groups is available in Private and Dedicated; hosted supports role maps but not direct AD group sync unless you use a SCIM connector.
[07:15] Priya: Encryption: at rest must be AES-256 with keys in our KMS, and in transit TLS 1.2+. Also HSM for some keys potentially.
[07:26] Maya: Bring-Your-Own-Key is supported and HSM integrations are available in the private appliance. We'll add KMS notes to the security pack.

[09:00] Daniel: About benchmarks — we can share an anonymized request trace to replay. Does Redwood have a replay harness or do we want synthetic?
[09:12] Maya: We do both. Replay gives closest fidelity but needs sanitized traces. Synthetic is faster for initial capacity checks. Proposal: Maya runs synthetic baseline first, then a replay run with your anonymized trace.
[09:30] Liam: That timeline works. How do you measure token accounting? We've had differences between vendor counters and our internal usage logs.
[09:42] Maya: We'll log model_version, input_tokens, output_tokens per request and provide a reconciliation spreadsheet. We'll also surface per-route cost in the console.

[11:10] Priya: Auditability: we need end-to-end traces for each request that show model version and any fallback events. If the service auto-fails over to a lower cost model, that must be recorded.
[11:24] Jordan: That's part of our graceful degradation story — we will capture fallback events in the audit stream and can tag them in the benchmark results.

[13:00] Daniel: For throughput tests, can you quantify tokens/sec per GPU for the model we plan to use (open-llama-13b-q)? We expect to evaluate a quantized 13B variant.
[13:12] Maya: Preliminary numbers for 13B-quant on A10G-like hardware are ~9k-14k tokens/sec for batched inferencing depending on batch size and sequence length. But we'll run the exact model build during the pilot to validate.
[13:40] Liam: We also need to confirm KV cache behavior for long conversations — we rely on persistent KV cache to avoid recomputing prefixes.
[13:53] Maya: Runtime supports KV cache and prefix caching; we'll show cache hit/miss stats in the bench dashboard. Note: cache persistence is simpler in Dedicated/Private.

[16:05] Priya: Legal/procurement: do you have a standard BAA? We'll need data processing addendum for regulated PII in EU and US. Also, data residency: our EU tenants must store logs in EU region.
[16:21] Jordan: We have a DPA and support region restrictions in Private deployments. For the pilot we can pin region to EU or do VPC peering into your EU region — we'll work with contracts.

[18:00] Daniel: Success criteria checklist idea: produce a runbook that includes 1) latency thresholds by payload type, 2) tokens/sec baseline, 3) accuracy baseline vs current model, 4) audit and log retention confirmation, 5) SSO/SCIM + RBAC integrated and verified.
[18:20] Maya: We'll draft that acceptance doc and circulate. Good to have signed off before the replay run.

[20:10] Priya: One more: alerting & observability. We require token-level cost alerts, model-drift alerts, and route error spike alarms pushed to our PagerDuty. Is that supported?
[20:26] Maya: Yes, Redwood Console supports per-route alerts and integration to PagerDuty/Webhooks. We'll map the alerting playbook to your thresholds as part of the POC.

[23:00] Liam: Timeline: we'd like to start pilot week of Feb 23, run two weeks of benching, then one week of integration tests, decision meeting by mid-March. Can you hit that?
[23:16] Jordan: Yes, if we get the anonymized traces and sign the DPA by Feb 18 we can schedule bench runs Feb 23-27 and replay week of Mar 1.

[25:40] Daniel: Small nit — we use an internal metric for token cost that includes infra overhead. Will you provide raw usage plus an estimated unit cost so we can compare apples-to-apples?
[25:55] Maya: We'll provide raw per-request token logs and a cost model spreadsheet with assumptions for GPU amortization and throughput.

[28:12] Priya: For SOC 2, we need a list of logical and physical controls you have in place and any third-party sub-processors. Also, scoping: do you encrypt logs at rest on SSDs?
[28:26] Maya: Yes, disks are encrypted; in hosted we use provider-managed encryption but in Private you can use your KMS. We'll include a sub-processor list.

[31:00] Jordan: Quick commercial note: for pilots we often offer a short, discounted POC pricing bracket and trial credits for bench runs. I'll include that in the follow-up.
[31:12] Liam: We appreciate that. Also want to flag procurement — procurement will want a clear SOW with acceptance criteria and an exit clause if the pilot fails.
[31:25] Jordan: Understood, we'll provide a proposed SOW template.

[34:00] Maya: On the technical run: I propose we run these bench phases — baseline synthetic (2 hours), burst/emulated traffic (3 hours), replay run (4 hours) — and capture p50/p95/p99, tokens/sec, cost-per-1k tokens and model-output diffs.
[34:18] Daniel: Sounds good. For replay we will anonymize user ids and strip any PII, then share S3 link.
[34:28] Priya: We need to see the log format beforehand to ensure retention and fields meet compliance.
[34:35] Maya: I'll attach a sample audit log JSON schema with the security pack.

[37:10] Liam: What about fallback policies? If a model variant fails, do you have circuit-breakers and automatic rollbacks?
[37:22] Maya: Yes, runtime supports canary rollouts, fallback to earlier model or lower-cost variant, and automatic throttling. We'll show a demo in the benchmarking walkthrough.

[39:40] Daniel: A small concern: we observed model version drift in vendor X where a minor update changed tokenization. How do you pin model versions and ensure deterministic behavior during replay?
[39:56] Maya: You can pin exact model artifacts and runtime container image. We store model hash and runtime hash in the audit logs to ensure deterministic replay.

[42:00] Priya: On RBAC: can you show an example of a role that has read-only for logs vs full admin?
[42:12] Maya: Yes, we'll provision two demo roles in the console during the integration: "audit-reader" and "infra-admin". We'll map those to SCIM groups or static role assignments.

[44:00] Jordan: Let's recap action items and owners. Maya will run synthetic bench and deliver results; Jordan will send security pack and SOW; Peregrine will provide anonymized traces and confirm retention needs.
[44:20] Liam: Good recap. Any final questions?
[44:30] Priya: One: GDPR — can you support data deletion requests within 48 hours for pilot data?
[44:38] Maya: Yes, we support deletion workflows; for Private deployments it's immediate, for hosted we have a documented erasure process and will include SLA in the pack.
[45:10] Jordan: We'll follow up with the security pack and schedule the bench. Thanks everyone, talk soon.

[47:00] Meeting ended.

Notes: transcription includes a few mis-heard tokens (e.g., "SOC two" -> "SOC two", "sam el" for SAML in one spot) and speaker overlaps. Bench numbers are preliminary.
